findings.text: Per-lruvec shrink driver repeatedly determines scan budget, optionally advances aging generation, evicts in bounded batches, aborts on protection or completion signals, and reports whether generation rotation is required for fairness.

Effective reclaim preference preserves anon-only mode, forces file-only when swapping is disallowed, and forces file-only when demotion is unavailable and swap space is below batch threshold; otherwise configured preference applies.

Generation advance first checks per-node mm tracking state; without tracking it advances directly, otherwise it requires completing a full mm iteration, using a no-walk path when hardware young-bit support or walk capability is absent.

Mm iteration serializes queue position and sequence under the mm list spin lock, initializes head on first use, extends tail and forces scan for newly added entries, accumulates stats while locked, and transfers mm reference to caller after unlock.
Bloom tracking uses sequence modulo filter count to select slot, allocates filter lazily on first use for that slot, and clears existing filter when a new pass starts with the first mm.

Mm tracking has build-dependent availability: enabled build provides per-cgroup list with global fallback and per-lruvec state with node-bitmap filtering and reference holding; disabled build provides null list, null state and no selectable mm.

Mm statistics accumulation requires holding mm list lock, folds walker-local counters into current history slot, clears walker counters, and on pass completion zeroes the next history slot when multiple history slots exist.
No-walk iteration advances mm sequence by one under lock only when supplied sequence is newer than recorded sequence, clearing queue anchors and reporting success; stale sequences report no work.

Address-space walk restarts from first user address, aborts if global max sequence moved, attempts non-blocking read lock on target mm, walks full range with skip test and batched accounting, flushes batches, and retries only on transient restart signal.

Batched page-count flush holds live lruvec interrupt-protected lock, drains per-generation type zone deltas into global generation counters, mirrors deltas into active or inactive compatibility sizes based on activeness, then releases lock.

Maximum sequence increment is single-winner: stale callers fail fast, winner ensures per-type generation count fits limit by advancing minima with reschedule and retry, rebalances compatibility sizes around old and new edges, refreshes control positions and timestamp, then publishes increment with release ordering.
Per-type generation count equals max minus min plus one and a valid lruvec keeps every type within configured minimum and maximum generation bounds.

Control position reset folds refaulted and protected plus evicted totals into running averages on carryover for the minimum sequence history slot, and zeroes refaulted evicted and protected counters for the relevant slot when history handling requires clearing.

Minimum sequence advance promotes every folio left in oldest generation to next generation while accounting protected amounts by reference tier, skips eligibility check for types excluded by swappiness mode, and returns incomplete when a bounded promotion budget is exhausted, leaving sequence unadvanced.

Folio generation promotion derives expected old generation from type minimum, preserves concurrent promotion by another path, otherwise atomically installs next generation and clears reference flags, and updates size accounting exactly once per successful install.

Eviction flushes empty oldest generations before and after isolation, isolates candidates then releases lruvec lock for shrink, handles writeback once per isolated set, reactivates rejected folios that remain in oldest generation, performs a second pass over unmapped clean folios, and updates demote steal and rotate statistics.

Empty-generation flushing and minimum-sequence publication require holding lruvec lock, skip work when no type advanced, clamp anon file skew around max minus minimum window when both types are evictable, then carry over control state and publish each advanced minimum.

Isolation scans an initial type tier choice and only switches to the other evictable type when the first type yielded no scan work; scanned but unisolated results keep focus on the same type to preserve controller bias, and report total scanned with selected type.

Generation accounting is dimensioned by generation count, anon and file type, and zone, with evictable-type iteration bounded by swappiness-derived lower and upper type limits and extremal min and max sequence snapshots taken with single-copy reads.

Advancing max while a type cannot advance min risks overlap between newest and oldest sequences causing cold hot inversion; code mitigates by skipping min advance for non-evictable types, clamping minima, and covering both sides of max when rebalancing compatibility sizes.
